items.question: Is ibuprofen safe to take?
items.reply: Ibuprofen is an NSAID used for pain, fever and inflammation [1.1]. The usual adult dose is 200 to 400 mg every 4 to 6 hours [1.2], and adults should not exceed 1,200 mg in 24 hours without a doctor's advice [1.3]. It should not be taken in the last three months of pregnancy [1.4]. It can cause stomach bleeding, especially in people over 65 [1.5]. If you are unsure, ask a pharmacist.

items.question: How do I fix a flat bike tyre?
items.reply: First remove the wheel from the frame [1.2]. Use tyre levers to lift one side of the tyre off the rim [1.3]. Pull out the old tube and check inside the tyre for thorns [1.4]. Slightly inflate the new tube and fit it inside the tyre [1.5]. Push the tyre back onto the rim and pump it to the pressure on the sidewall, usually 80 to 100 psi for a road bike [1.6]. Never use a screwdriver, because it can puncture the new tube [1.7].
